gaps.sentence: There are cases ___ this rule simply does not apply.
gaps.explanation: 'Cases where ...' means 'cases in which ...'; 'that' cannot introduce the clause without a subject.
'What I meant' means 'the thing that I meant'; 'that I meant' would be an incomplete relative clause.

gaps.sentence: The company's shares, ___ rose sharply yesterday, are still undervalued.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to the shares; 'that' is impossible in a clause set off by commas.

gaps.sentence: The shower suddenly stopped working, ___ meant we had to call a plumber.
gaps.hint: refers back to the whole event
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to the whole preceding clause; 'what' cannot introduce this kind of clause after a comma.

gaps.sentence: It was the first time ___ I had ever driven on my own.
gaps.hint: after 'the first time', use this pronoun
gaps.explanation: 'The first time that ...' is the standard pattern; the pronoun may also be omitted, but 'which' and 'what' do not fit.

gaps.sentence: That's the office ___ I worked for ten years.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' means 'in which'; 'I worked the office' shows the place role of the gap.

gaps.sentence: The programme ___ I watched last night was about volcanoes.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to things, even when it is the object of the clause.

gaps.sentence: I've told you everything ___ you need to know.
gaps.explanation: After 'everything', 'that' is used (and may be omitted); 'which' is avoided after 'everything'.
